title: SalahOS Muhkam/Mutashabih divine-attribute coverage
scope: Full-corpus lexical/contextual audit of the 6,236-ayah corpus for the anthropomorphic, bodily, spatial, directional and created-quality risk families governed by the project-owner Muhkam/Mutashabih guide. This is not a claim that every kind of mutashabih matter has a humanly knowable ta'wil; the guide itself distinguishes matters whose exact reality/timing is known only to Allah.
rules: Muhkam foundations govern every mutashabih rendering.
Never render Allah with bodily, spatial, directional, created, sensuous or human modality.
Use tafwid with tanzih where a specific gloss is not established.
Use contextual ta'wil only for the verse/context in which it is supported; never turn one ta'wil into a universal lexical substitution.

categories.description: All seven Qur'anic occurrences of istawa 'ala al-'Arsh.
Occurrences of istawa ila al-sama that must not be rendered as bodily turning or movement.
Divine wajh expressions: qiblah, acceptance/pleasure, Self or Dominion according to context; never a bodily face.
Divine yad/yadayn/yamin expressions: power, care, bounty, dominion or generosity according to context; never bodily hands.
Divine 'ayn/a'yun expressions rendered as care, protection or watchfulness; never bodily eyes.
Ruh attributed to Allah is created and/or an attribution of honour/command; never a part of Allah.
Divine ma'iyyah rendered by knowledge, support or protection according to context; never physical co-location.
Fawq expressions concerning Allah rendered as supremacy/subjugation or authority; never physical direction.
Fi al-sama wording must not place Allah inside the sky; render supreme status/dominion without location.
Coming expressions concerning Allah rendered contextually as judgment, command, punishment or an indication of power; never locomotion.
Ascension/raising wording must not imply movement to a place occupied by Allah.
Nur attributed to Allah rendered as guidance/revelation where context supports it; never physical luminosity.
Bayt attributed to Allah is an attribution of honour, never residence or containment.
Kursi is retained without translating it as a bodily seat; no place or containment is implied.
Nearness wording is rendered through knowledge/care or created agents according to context, not spatial distance.
Statements liable to imply Allah is physically in heaven/earth are rendered without location.
Allah coming between a person and heart is rendered as control over the person and heart, not spatial insertion.
Ihatah is rendered as comprehensive knowledge where the supplied guide gives that meaning, not bodily surrounding.
Going 'to my Lord' is rendered as going where Allah commanded, not travelling to Allah's location.
Saq in 68:42 is rendered as hardship/anguish according to the guide, never a bodily shin.
